Elena / Rafael — I put together three quick scenarios in the attached workbook (insightai_cost-model.xlsx):

Scenario A — Hosted API (pay-per-token):
- Baseline per-token rates applied for gen + input tokens.
- No reserved capacity; scaling handled by Redwood routing.
- Pros: zero commit, fastest time to market. 
- Cons: higher unit cost at scale, less predictability for budgeting.

Scenario B — Dedicated (reserved commit):
- Three commit tiers included (medium, large, x-large) with monthly GPU pool pricing.
- Model-level quantization (8-bit) and continuous KV caching assumed — ~25-40% token cost reduction vs Hosted at comparable latency.
- Pros: predictable monthly invoice, improved unit economics for steady traffic and high concurrency.
- Cons: commit required; need usage smoothing strategy.

Scenario C — Private VPC (customer-managed):
- Includes 1) private control plane + network costs and 2) optional on-prem SKU.
- Higher setup costs and TAC for HSM/KMS integrations.
- Pros: max data isolation; preferred for some regulated customers.

I included a sensitivity table showing break-even points for Dedicated vs Hosted at varying commit levels and burst patterns. Two quick open questions for InsightAI: 
1) For monthly commit planning, can you share expected minimum committed throughput (if you have a target)?
2) Are there internal finance rules around capex vs opex we should be aware of (this affects whether Dedicated or Private is preferred)?

I’ll be standing by to walk the procurement team through the workbook.
